Since digital circuits operate on the premise of two states (on or off) those states can easily be represented numerically using binary.
INTRODUCTIONM
Many digital devices must interface with the world of humans which think and operate on the decimal system.
Therefore, some form of translation must be established between the base 10 human world and the base 2 digital world. This is the job of encoder circuits.
Let's begin the lesson on BASE 10 TO BINARY CONVERSION....................
LESSON MENU
DECIMAL ENCODERITLE
The decimal encoder circuit converts decimal numbers to outputs that represent binary numbers, in this example BCD (binary coded decimal).
DISCUSSION
On the outputs of the OR gates are LED's. When a gate outputs a logic high the diode is forward-biased and it illuminates...
If an OR gate output is LOW, the correlating diode is reversed-biased and does not illuminate.
Notice that the decimal inputs lack the number "0". This is because the OR gate outputs are all low when there are not high inputs..
The Truth Table to the right of the encoder illustrates the binary count based upon any given input.
Since BCD numbers cannot, by design, exceed 9 (1001), the truth table reflects only a binary count from 0-9.
We know from our OR gate theory that any HIGH into an OR gate will cause the gate to output a HIGH.

Simple encoders such as the one just examined have a drawback. Suppose input lines 7 and 8 are simultaneously brought to a logic high.
This presents two problems. First this will illuminate all four LEDs which is not the appropriate output for either input.
Secondly, with all four LED's illuminated, a binary 15 is being displayed. BCD code cannot have any number greater than 9.
Clearly, this is a problem. In order to get around this, an altered version called a Priority Encoder was developed.han 9.
The schematic below is an 74147 Priority Encoder. Priority Encoders include circuitry that force the output to reflect only the highest order input when two or more inputs are active.
For example, if input lines 4 & 5 are active at the same time, only the output corresponding to line 5 will be reflected.ly the highest order input when two or more inputs are active.

BASE 10 TO BINARY CONVERSION

This experiment demonstrates the operation of a decimal to binary encoder circuit. You will enter a decimal number and probe the outputs of the encoder to verify the correct outputs of HIGH and LOW signals exist.
EXPERIMENT
Pick up the PC130-108 card. The purpose of this card is to encode a decimal number for a three LED binary display.
Notice the PC130-108 has only 7 input switches. This should not be understood to imply an octal encoder. Due to limited space on the circuit card, only decimal inputs 1 - 7 were included.
Switches 1 through 7 are used to apply the decimal numbers
Gates A, B and C are used to convert the decimal number to a value used to represent the equivalent binary number.
Note, the NOT function is connected to the input signals of the OR gates.
These gates are called inhibited OR gates. The logic produced is the same as a NAND gate.
With all switches set to HI, the outputs of gates A, B and C are LOW.
With switch 5 set to LO, the output of gates A and C are HIGH. LEDs 4 and 1 illuminate.
The binary number 101 equals the decimal number 5. Let's begin the experiment.
